claim: When an LLM lacks a clear signal from training data, it generates a statistically likely continuation that is often confident and wrong.

evidence.quote: LLMs predict the next token based on statistical patterns learned during training — they do not “know” facts, they approximate them. When the model lacks a clear signal from training data, it generates the most statistically likely continuation — which is often confident and wrong.
evidence.source_title: LLM Hallucinations: Why They Happen and How to Reduce Them [2026]
